newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Liddell reaches accord on Korea coal exports.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Liddell reaches accord on Korea coal exports.

text.p: Liddell Coal Operation Pty Ltd said on Wednesday it had reached agreement on price with Korea Electric Power Co (KEPCO) for coal to be supplied in 1997 and the accord would set the price for other Australian exporters.

Liddell, a joint venture of Savage Resources Ltd and Mitsui Matsushima's Australian unit, did not announce the price agreed with KEPCO but said it represented a US$2.67 per tonne decrease from the 1996 price.

Marketing general manager Robin Boyer said in a news release that "although the price agreed was a decrease of US$2.67 per tonne from the 1996 level, this is quite satisfactory given the current market conditions and previous speculation that KEPCO may require a much greater discount".
The price compared with a US$2.65 reduction to US$37.65 a tonne in the Japanese benchmark price for 1997.
Liddell said KEPCO was one of Asia's largest coal consumers with current annual consumption of 20 million tonnes.
Liddell has a 10-year contract to supply 400,000 tonnes per year to KEPCO and was selected by KEPCO as the Australian lead negotiator for the 1997 price.
Korea is Australia's second coal export market after Japan.
Boyer said: "With the commissioning of the new Glendell open cut mine, Liddell is increasing production this year to about 2.7 million tonnes, about 2.0 million tonnes saleable.
"This will increase to 5.0 million tonnes and will provide prime quality thermal and semi soft coking coal for many years to come."
